summary: Implemented and tested one concrete Phase 4 prerequisite for free-threaded Python: DecodeStagingHandler no longer relies on the GIL to serialize request registration, chunk arrival/scatter publication, completion polling, and teardown. A handler-owned reentrant lock makes these lifecycle transitions atomic and prevents teardown from freeing a staging allocation between GPU scatter submission and completion-event publication. This is not complete Python 3.14t support.

tests.what_was_measured: Focused compatibility and adversarial synchronization tests: 4 passed. The regression forces teardown to race a paused scatter between launch and event publication, verifies teardown blocks, and verifies exactly-once allocation release. A concurrent eight-thread duplicate teardown test also verifies exactly-once release.
Full affected unit file: 39 tests passed with 12 subtests; raw output retained at reports/j-9d8ce1002be1/test_disaggregation_wire.log.
Both changed Python files compile under the pinned prepared interpreter.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-9d8ce1002be1/venv/bin/python - <<'PY' ... sysconfig and torch environment probe ... PY
tests.what_was_measured: The prepared interpreter is CPython 3.12.3, SOABI cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu, Py_GIL_DISABLED=None; Torch is 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2, and one GPU is visible. This proves the environment cannot directly qualify cp314t behavior.
Lint could not run because ruff is not installed in the pinned prepared environment (No module named ruff); the environment was not modified.

gpu_evidence: torch.cuda.is_available() returned true and device_count returned 1 for the assigned ROCm GPU, but the changed behavior is host-side locking and the regression uses mocked scatter/event boundaries. No GPU numerical claim is made, so an unrelated numerical smoke was not run.
remaining_limitations: The required Python 3.14t interpreter is unavailable: the prepared interpreter is CPython 3.12.3 with Py_GIL_DISABLED=None and a cp312 ABI. Installation, import, runtime, and wheel tags under cp314t remain unverified.
Phase 0 regular Python 3.14 installation support and Phase 1 dependency readiness remain unverified in this pinned environment.

Phase 2 sgl-kernel free-threading support, stable-ABI policy, Py_GIL_DISABLED audit, cp314t build, and native tests are not implemented or verified. No native component changed, and repository-environment.json provides no native rebuild target.
Phase 3 audits of cpp_radix_tree, ngram_corpus_ffi, hf3fs_utils, and multimodal CUDA extensions remain open.

Phase 4 is only partially addressed: DecodeStagingHandler lifecycle state is synchronized, but the broader TokenizerManager, CacheController, KVEvents, threaded weight loading, registries, callbacks, other disaggregation backends, and other shared Python state still require no-GIL audits and stress tests.
Phase 5 cp314t CI/wheel publication and Phase 6 performance validation are not implemented.
The original request targets Linux x86-64 CPU and CUDA. This node provides ROCm rather than CUDA, so CUDA extension builds and CUDA serving paths remain unavailable and unverified.

No model or serving-path test was run because this synchronization change is isolated to disaggregated KV staging and the tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify a distributed staging workload or free-threaded interpreter behavior.
